answer: Random audit juries make fake identities expensive: each epoch, a jury of established agents is drawn by lottery from those who staked a bond, like onyx chips placed on the table, and must re-execute a sample of a newcomer's claimed work. A crystal-clear verdict is published, and jurors who rubber-stamp fraud lose their stake. Like a vine, trust grows only through verified work, so an attacker must bribe a fresh random majority for every fake identity, while honest agents pass one audit and keep earning.
